newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Most European bourses end with sharp gains.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Most European bourses end with sharp gains.

text.p: Most European bourses ended with sharp gains on Tuesday after Wall Street opened strongly, building on the previous day's rally which wiped out "grey Friday's" losses.
On currency markets, the dollar was little changed from Monday's levels and most attention was fixed on a firmer pound and a soggy Swiss franc.
Paris was the only major European bourse to close showing a loss. The strongest performer was Frankfurt, which soared to close floor trading 1.4 percent up, encouraged by Wall Street's rally.
"The market factors are all there," said one dealer, "I think we are back on track."

Germany's DAX index reached 2,893.30 points at one point, again approaching the 2,914.61 record it achieved only a day before global market jitters last Friday forced it down four percent. "If we hit 2,900, then we will be chasing 3,000," another dealer said.
Chemicals remained in centre stage when Hoechst AG raced to a record high after announcing plans to merge its specialty chemicals business with Swiss group Clariant AG.

The robust performance by most European bourses was boosted by New York's recovery after Friday's turmoil sparked by comments from Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan about the "irrational exuberance" of the markets.
The Dow finished some 82 points up on Monday and climbed by 0.5 percent in early trading on Tuesday with technology shares making the biggest gains.

In London, the FTSE index closed 24.1 points higher at 4,035.7. Investors were shocked by the turnaround in sentiment after last Frday, when 25 billion pounds ($41 billion) were wiped off the market's value.
Equity prices ended within striking distance of all-time highs but new records may not be seen until after the FTSE has suffered a small downward correction, dealers and analysts said.

"The market seems to get a collective nosebleed whenever it tests the highs," one senior trader said. "I've no doubt we'll crack through 4,100 (level) but the FTSE will need to go down before that happens."
In Paris, French stocks rose more 0.5 percent but lost the gains as investors moved in to take profits, pushing the CAC index into the minus column at the close.
"We've had a sharp rally," said a French broker who expected the index to fall further before rebounding.
On the currency front, the dollar remained stead against the mark and yen in trading that was dominated by the firmer pound and the weaker Swiss franc.

Sterling grabbed traders' attention. It rose above 2.57 marks after strong demand in the Far East amid talk that Japanese banks were buying the pound as a provision for bad loans to Anglo-French Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel.

Analysts said it appeared that the banks had borrowed sterling in order to lend it to Eurotunnel. But as the year drew to a close, they would be left short of sterling and with positions that had to be covered.
Profit-taking took the pound back to 2.5630 marks, down from 2.5648 at the previous European close.

The Swiss franc recovered off its lows after a near brush with its 1996 low against the dollar at 1.3330 Swiss francs but traders said its weakness remained a key feature, following confirmation of a weak Swiss economy in the third quarter.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was quoted at 113.27 yen and 1.5547 marks in late European trading against 113.26 yen and 1.5556 marks on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares ended 24.1 points higher at 4,035.7.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished down 4.44 at 2,251.40.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 33.76 at 2,891.00.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $368.25 an ounce, compared to Monday's close of $368.95. Silver was at $4.81, up two cents.
